sources.note: Detects flawed reasoning from residual-stream trajectories by combining layerwise motion with a quantized region reader and a normalized direction reader, rather than probing full states.
sources.title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs

sources.note: Reads reasoning validity from layer-to-layer displacement of hidden states rather than from the states themselves, on the grounds that static activations let probes latch onto lexical surface patterns.
sources.title: Truth as a Trajectory: What Internal Representations Reveal About Large Language Model Reasoning

sources.note: Explains LLM counting failures as a depth limit, since counting is computed across layers, and fixes it with a System-2 decomposition whose mechanism is then traced.
sources.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Large-Scale Counting in LLMs through a System-2 Strategy

sources.note: Characterizes exactly how much computational power a chain of thought buys as a function of its length, sandwiching the class of languages a decoder recognizes with t(n) decoding steps between two standard complexity classes.
sources.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought

sources.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
sources.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

sources.note: Proves a tighter no-CoT upper bound of AC^0 for constant-precision transformers, and shows T steps of chain of thought let a constant-depth model compute anything a size-T boolean circuit can.
sources.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems

sources.note: Reads a reasoning trajectory as a multi-step pseudo-gradient descent on the model's own parameters, which makes each token an optimization step, the trajectory an inner loop, and the training regime a meta-learning problem in which the question is the task.
sources.title: Deciphering Trajectory-Aided LLM Reasoning: An Optimization Perspective

sources.note: Proves that reasoning can be moved from emitted tokens into hidden states without losing sample efficiency, using a curriculum that deletes thinking tokens in geometric chunks and so needs only logarithmically many training stages.
sources.title: Transformers Provably Learn to Internalize Chain-of-Thought

sources.note: Proves via circuit complexity that bounded-depth Transformers cannot directly solve basic arithmetic, linear equations or general dynamic programming unless their size grows super-polynomially, while constant-size autoregressive Transformers can solve all of them by generating chain-of-thought derivations.
sources.title: Towards Revealing the Mystery behind Chain of Thought: A Theoretical Perspective

result.definition: How much of a network's depth a computation actually uses, and across 9 sources a quantity that appears in three different literatures with the same shape. Theoretically it is the thing chain of thought buys: a bounded-depth transformer is limited by its layers in one forward pass, and emitting intermediate tokens converts sequence length into effective depth, which is why the number of steps maps onto complexity classes. Empirically it appears as depth-localisation -- grounding detection climbing through early layers, peaking mid-network and falling toward the output; the useful read-out band being narrow and mid-network; and reasoning-relevant signals concentrated in particular layers rather than spread. And as a mechanism it appears in the counting work, where latent counts are stored, transferred through dedicated heads and aggregated at the final stage, which is a depth-structured computation rather than a distributed one. The archive's practical consequence is that pooling across depth dilutes rather than aggregates, and that a claim about where a computation lives needs the layer sweep rather than a single site.
